title: Teach, notice and return
text: Sequence. Pupil textbook pages 1-6: classroom purpose; two-to-none demonstration and the meaning of 0; guided one-to-none, recognition, numeral formation and empty-box drawing; independent source tasks; recall/support; actual packing resolution and fresh checks. Use the existing book introductions; this continuation does not repeat them.

Prepare. Large safe counters, reachable tray/mat, storage box, pencil/paper and ordinary cards 0-5. Demonstrate each physical action. The trays/boxes in exact diagrams are containers, not counted tops. Never count decorative classroom artwork. No subtraction or equality notation is needed in these pupil pages.

Notice. Separate empty-set meaning, recognition, independently naming a numeral, and writing without copying. A child may count the tray as one: ask what is being counted, then inspect its contents. An open or reversed loop needs formation practice, not a judgement that the child cannot understand none. Accept usual communication for naming; use an established adapted writing method where needed.

Intervene, then recheck. Use one counter and another container. Model moving it away and checking the contents. Link none to 0. Recheck independently with two counters and a fresh tray, both put away: zero remain. For writing, air-write and trace a large closed loop, cover the model, then dictate zero on blank paper. Give specific feedback and retry later.

Delayed recall. Next session put three counters in a different basket, then ask the pupil to put all away: zero remain. Mix cards 2,0,4: independently name two, zero, four without an adult supplying the names. Cover them and dictate zero: write 0. Record meaning, recognition, naming and formation separately; give further supported practice if needed.

title: Answers and fresh checks
text:
Source questions, unchanged meaning/order.
P1-03-Q1 (TB4/WB1): 0 tops in the empty set.
Q2 (TB4/WB1): a closed box outline with nothing inside; acceptable neat alternatives.
Q3 (TB4/WB2): missing numeral 2 in 0,1,2,3.
Q4 (TB5/WB3): all three put away; 0 remain.
Q5 (TB5/WB3): say zero, using usual communication if needed.
Q6 (TB5/WB3): no oranges are inside the basket; the basket exists.

Models/guided (TB2-3/WB1-2). Two tops before moving, zero after. One top moved away leaves zero. Choose 0 among cards 0,2,1. Closed oval for 0; arrow shows downward direction on the left. Empty-box outline is a model, not a writing space in the textbook. Real quantity sequence none/one/two/three matches 0/1/2/3. WB1 completed example: 1 top, written numeral 1.

Recall/support/ending (TB5-6/WB3). Recall: no objects inside. Support: one then two counters moved away, zero remain. Ending: zero on mat, three stored; actually move counters and check the mat before closure. Count stored objects once each; no objects are lost or added.

Fresh checks (TB6/WB4). Privately prepare trays with 0,2,4 safe counters; change positions. Empty tray contains 0. Write 0 without copying. Shuffle cards 0-5 (no fixed order); ask recognition by naming a card, then independently test reading by pointing without saying its name, including 0 and two other values. Before dictation, cover all cards and earlier written/printed numerals, including the first count answer on WB4. Then dictate zero. WB4 records separate recognition/reading/writing results; repeated tasks on two surfaces are one assessment, not two.
Do not prompt an answer before a naming check. Vary tray positions and card order. Compare observable actions with the rubric; these activities have not been administered to pupils.

title: Teach, notice and return
text: Sequence. TB1 purpose; TB2-3 quantities six/seven then eight/nine, numeral names and one-to-one counting; TB4 live formation/air-writing; TB5 actual sorting; TB6 modelled quantity order and source tasks; TB7 drawing model, recall/support; TB8 actual sorting/counting/ordering resolution, then fresh checks. Do not advance before each quantity is secure. Existing introductions remain in the opening book.

Prepare. Reachable mats, large safe counters, paper/pencil and cards 1-9. For S002 prepare 6 blue circles, 7 red squares, 8 green triangles and 9 yellow non-square rectangles. Model sorting by outline; shape naming is not assessed. Printed pieces use one colour to show the outline rule. All 30 pieces stay in the same four story groups. Squares remain a special kind of rectangle; use the most specific names here.

Separate skills. Observe quantity, count-once method, recognition, independent naming, dictation/formation and order separately. Counting correctly does not prove reading; copying does not prove writing from dictation. For reversed 6 or 9, keep paper upright and watch the loop/downstroke. Accept usual communication and established adapted writing methods.

Support/recheck. Use counted/uncounted mats and five counters plus one. Model six, then independently check a new seven set. If sorting is hard, sort two small groups then rebuild the target groups. For numeral difficulty, air-write/trace one form, cover it, then dictate it; later retry a different order. Do not label a child as the weak counter.

Delayed recall, next session. Count fresh sets of 6, 7 and 8. Read shuffled cards 9, 6, 8, 7 independently. Dictate nine, seven, six, eight: 9, 7, 6, 8. Order 8, 6, 9: 6, 8, 9. Sort 7 tops and 9 leaves; state each count. Record which skills need support.

title: Answers and independent checks
text: Source tasks. P1-04-Q1 (TB6/WB2): 7. Q2 (same): 8. Q3 (same): 6, 7, 8, 9. Q4 (TB7/WB3): exactly 6 separate dots, any clear arrangement. Q5 (same): exactly 9 real objects, each counted once; state 9. Q6 (TB7/WB4): recount 8 once per object; the last word is eight. Moving each counted object is valid. Check the method as well as the total.

Every model. TB2: 6 is five and one; 7 is five and two. TB3: 8 is five and three; 9 is five and four. Spreading changes no quantity. TB4/WB1: recognisable 6, 7, 8, 9; loop below for 6, above for 9. TB5: 6 round/7 square; guided 8 triangle/9 rectangle. TB6: pairing 6 and 7 leaves one unmatched in 7; seven goes between six and eight. Before/after mean earlier/later in counting order. TB7: 2 counters/2 dots; support 6, recheck 7. TB8: groups of 6, 7, 8, 9 in increasing row order.

S002 (TB5/WB5). Mix all 30 pieces. Sort by outline, count and record: 6 circles, 7 squares, 8 triangles, 9 non-square rectangles. Order: 6, 7, 8, 9. Observe actual sorting; written counts alone do not demonstrate it. For story closure (TB8), verify all 30 pieces in these groups before starting the pretend game.

Fresh checks (TB8/WB6). Privately prepare new scattered groups of 8 and 9; answers 8 and 9. S003: count 9 objects once each, then independently name ALL shuffled cards 1-9 without supplied names. Test recognition separately by naming 6, 7, 8, 9 in a different order. Before dictation, cover ALL cards, printed numerals and the pupil's handwritten count answers, including the totals on WB6. S004: dictate eight, six, nine, seven; answers 8, 6, 9, 7, correctly oriented. Do not show answers or read this rubric aloud while testing.
Same tasks on both surfaces count as one check. New physical objects, independently shuffled naming and covered-model dictation are fresh evidence. No tasks have been administered to pupils.

title: Teach, notice and return
text: Progression. TB1 purpose; TB2 ten ones, bundle/unbundle without changing quantity; TB3 tens on left/ones on right; TB4-5 gradual building/naming of every number 11-20; TB6 live formation/reading; TB7-8 source tasks; TB9 recall/support; TB10 actual packing and fresh checks. Do not rush a ladder page as one lesson. Teach each number with real materials before proceeding.

Prepare. Large paper strips, loose bands, reachable trays/box, pencil/paper and ordinary cards 10-20. Keep 20 strips for the story; use extra demonstration strips or return all story strips before closure. Every tied ten contains exactly 10 visible/countable strips. The band is not one of the counted strips. Open bundles to verify rather than trusting labels or decorative art.

Observe separately. Does the pupil count each one once, make exactly ten, preserve quantity on tying/untying, read shuffled numerals, place digits correctly and explain zero loose ones in 20? One bundle is one ten, not one one. The left digit counts tens, the right counts loose ones. For 10 versus 1, compare actual ten strips with one strip. Accept usual communication and established adapted writing methods.

Help and fresh recheck. Count 9 then one more, recount 10, tie and open. Privately prepare a different set of 11 or 13 strips. Ask for complete tens and loose ones, then a record: 11 gives 1 ten/1 one; 13 gives 1 ten/3 ones. Give no answer before the attempt. For handwriting, model one two-digit numeral, cover all models and prior answers, then dictate a different one on fresh space.

Delayed recall. Next session build 18 (1 ten and 8 ones) and 10 (1 ten and 0 ones). Read shuffled 19, 12, 20, 11. Cover cards and every prior written/printed numeral, then dictate fifteen, twenty, eleven: 15, 20, 11. Record distinct skill results and revisit difficulties.

title: Answers and fresh checks
text: Source questions. P1-05-Q1 (TB7/WB2): 12. Q2 (same): 1 ten and 6 ones. Q3 (same): 10 ones. Q4 (TB8/WB4): 19. Q5 (same): 2 bundles, exactly 10 ones in each; 20 total. Q6 (same): ten has 10 ones; one has 1 one. An opened real bundle or accurate pointing/explanation is acceptable.

All models/practice. TB2: 10 loose becomes one ten, still 10 after untying. TB3: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones; guided 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones. TB4: 11-15 have 1 ten and 1-5 loose ones respectively. TB5: 16-19 have 1 ten and 6-9 ones respectively; 20 has 2 tens and 0 ones. TB6 cards name eighteen, eleven, twenty, sixteen. WB1: 10 ones; two tens and no loose ones make 20. WB3: form 10, 14, 20. Digits must be recognisable and in order.

Recall/choice/support/ending. TB9/WB5: open/count 10 once each. Any chosen 11-19 is valid: 1 ten and the remaining 1-9 ones; written numeral, real strips and recorded digits must agree. Support/recheck is described on TB11. TB10 ending uses the original 20 markers: exactly 10 in each of 2 bundles, no loose ones. Actually pack/check before closure.

Fresh checks (TB10/WB6). Privately ask pupil to build 17 and 20: 1 ten/7 ones and 2 tens/0 ones; open/recount to check. Shuffle ALL cards 10-20 for independent naming without supplied names. Test recognition separately by naming 10, 16, 20 in a different order. Before dictation cover ALL cards, printed numerals and earlier handwritten answers, including WB6 build records. Dictate nineteen, ten, fourteen, twenty: 19, 10, 14, 20. Do not show this rubric while testing.
Repeated tasks on two surfaces are one check. Models are not fresh assessment evidence. Variable pupil-built sets require observation. No classroom outcomes are asserted.

title: Words, evidence and credits
text: Words. One: a single item here. Ones/units: single items. A ten contains ten ones; the ones place records loose ones. Bundle of ten: exactly ten ones held together. Tens place: the left position in our two-digit numbers; ones place: the right. Zero ones: no loose ones. Eleven to nineteen: one ten and one to nine extra ones. Twenty: two tens.

Historical mapping. P1-p02-06: recognise ten objects as one group. P1-p02-07: tens/ones with activities extending to 20. Stable P1-05-Q1-Q6 prompts, answers and order retained. title: A fair paper display
text:
Equal parts.
Fair shares.

Aishatu: My box-toy display needs one paper mat. Each of us wants the same space for a drawing. I want to start now!
Mrs Binta: First let us learn to share the whole mat fairly.
Adamu: Nobody should be left out.
Grace: I will check the edges neatly.
John: Let me try a fold before you tell me.
We will make and recognise equal halves and quarters. Keep paper on a reachable table. Use scrap paper instead of food.

title: Watch the paper fold
text: Mrs Binta: This complete sheet is one whole. Watch me bring one short edge exactly onto the other. Press the fold. Open the sheet.
The line shows the fold. The two pieces cover the same amount of paper. Fold again to check that they fit exactly on each other. Equal means the same amount of space here.
Each part is a half of the whole. Two equal halves make the whole. I shade one part on my paper: one half is shaded.
Try together. Take a rectangle of scrap paper. Match its short edges, fold and open. Touch each half. Say, "Two equal parts." Turn the sheet. Is each part still a half?
Grace: Turning the sheet changes its direction. It does not change the amount of paper in each half. Keep your folded sheet for the next turn.

title: Fold again for quarters
text: Mrs Binta: Watch with a square sheet. Match opposite edges and fold in half. Keep it folded. Match the other pair of edges and fold once more. Open all the folds.
There are four equal parts. Each part is a quarter of the whole. Four equal quarters make the whole. I shade just one part: one quarter is shaded.
Try together. Fold your own square in half, then fold it in half again the other way. Open it. Touch and count the four equal parts. Shade one part on your paper.
Adamu: I count four parts. Mrs Binta: Check the amount too. Fold them onto each other: they must fit. Four pieces alone do not prove that they are quarters.

title: Check the amount, not just the count
text:
Aishatu: I drew a quick line. Two pieces must be halves!
Mrs Binta: Check them. One has less paper. Two unequal pieces are not halves.
John: The right whole has two equal parts. Each is a half. Aishatu tries again and matches the edges before pressing the fold.
A new way: I draw a line from one corner of a square to the opposite corner. The two triangles fit exactly on each other when folded. Each triangle is a half.
Try together. On paper, copy the square and corner-to-corner line. Point to a half. Explain how the pieces match. Workbook: Check the parts.

title: Turn it and name the part
text: Mrs Binta: Watch me turn a square without changing its pieces. In the tilted square, four equal triangles meet in the middle. One shaded triangle is a quarter.
The paper orange model also has two equal parts. One part is a half. It is paper, not food. Fold a round paper model through its centre to check the matching halves.
Say together: a half is one of two equal parts; a quarter is one of four equal parts. Shape and direction may change. Equal amounts still matter.
Mrs Binta: Now we can read short names. 1/2 is read "one half": one of two equal parts. 1/4 is read "one quarter": one of four equal parts. Say the words as I point. You may answer in words.

title: Watch me draw and shade
text: Mrs Binta: Watch me draw a rectangle on paper. I mark the middle of the top and bottom edges. I join the marks with a straight line. This makes two equal halves.
Use a folded paper edge to find the middle. Check by folding the two parts onto each other.
Watch me draw a square. I draw one line through the middle from top to bottom, then another from side to side. I count four equal parts. I shade just one.

Grace: A smudge crossed my line. I will try again on spare paper.
Mrs Binta: Neatness helps us see the parts. You can point and explain too.
Try together on paper: draw the rectangle, then the square. Check before shading.

title: Complete answers and observation
text: Source questions (textbook p7; workbook pp2-3). Q1: 2 equal parts. Q2: 4 equal parts. Q3: rectangle divided into two equal-area parts; middle vertical/horizontal or corner-to-corner diagonal accepted. Q4: square with four equal-area parts, exactly one shaded; grid or four centre-meeting triangles accepted. Q5: No; unequal amounts are not halves. Q6: whole has four equal parts and exactly one is shaded. Accept equivalent spoken wording.

Models and guided turns (textbook pp2-6; workbook p1). HALF: two matching equal parts, unchanged when turned. QUARTER: four matching parts after perpendicular folds, one shaded. COMPARE: left .3/.7 unequal, right .5/.5 halves. DIAGONAL: two equal triangles each half. ROTATED: four equal triangles, one shaded quarter. FRUIT: two equal parts, one shaded half. NOTATION: 1/2 one half; 1/4 one quarter. DRAW: rectangle middle line; square middle cross with one part shaded. Workbook p1: top-left half, top-right quarter; bottom-left no, bottom-right yes. Require amount as well as count.

Support, recheck and extension (textbook p8; workbook p4). Helped rectangle: two equal halves. New tall rectangle: one middle line makes equal halves; new square: four equal parts, one indicated quarter. A different half may be horizontal, vertical or diagonal. Test equal area by folding/overlay, not matching shape alone; different-shaped pieces can also have equal area. Adults may verify other mathematically valid partitions.

title: Story, fresh checks and delayed recall
text: Story (textbook p9; workbook p5). One square whole, four equal quarters, one drawing per friend. Four quarters exhaust the whole with no overlap. Names on textbook mat: Aishatu upper-left, Adamu upper-right, Grace lower-left, John lower-right. Workbook may place names or drawings in any order. Require one equal share for each, no excluded friend.

Fresh tasks (textbook p10; workbook p6). Left: half, two equal parts, one shaded despite rotation. Middle paper fruit: quarter, four equal parts, one shaded. Right: neither, two unequal parts (.3/.7); shading alone does not name a fraction. New drawing: four equal-area parts of a whole with exactly one shaded. Recall: half one of two equal parts; quarter one of four equal parts.

Intervene, then new recheck. If counting alone: overlap unequal paper pieces to show unequal space. Match folded edges before naming halves. If all shaded parts called quarters: compare equal two-part and equal four-part wholes, touching each part. If rotation confuses: turn the same sheet slowly. After help, give a NEW wide rectangle for halves and NEW square for quarters. Do not score coached work as independent.

Delayed recall next session. With blank paper and no models, ask the pupil to make equal halves of a new rectangle and quarters of a new square, point to one part of each and explain. Present a square split diagonally and a paper orange split into unequal pieces: half; not halves. Check again in later weeks with different orientations. Record assistance.

text: Teach one new missing-number position at a time. Revisit addition and subtraction with counters before this chapter. Read all prompts aloud. Introduce - as take away and + as join; = means equal amounts. A blank represents a number, not an instruction to calculate everything on its left.

title: Adult guide: prepare and observe
text: Four historical objectives. Recognise genuine denominations; combine values through 25k; find change from payments through 10k; rub genuine coin surfaces through brown and white paper. Pretend arithmetic does not establish genuine-coin identification. All real-resource stages are conditional opportunities, not recorded pupil outcomes.

text: Routes and sequence. Textbook 1 story/goal; 2 values; 3 genuine model/guided to workbook 1; 4 rubbing to workbook 2; 5 totals; 6 change; 7-9 independent originals to workbook 3-5; 10 recall BEFORE help; 11-14 help and new rechecks; 15 closure; 16 fresh to workbook 6-7. title: Try a real coin rubbing
